3. Consult residents twice a year, incorporating genuine preference into the next menu cycle where practicable.
4. Update a resident's dietary or allergen record immediately if their needs change, communicating this to the kitchen the same day.

Exceptions and professional judgement

Where a resident's dietary need changes suddenly (for example, a new allergy identified by their GP), the kitchen adapts that resident's meals immediately rather than waiting for the next scheduled menu review to reflect the change.

Local and regional variations

A site with a more culturally diverse resident group tailors its rotating menu to include a wider range of culturally appropriate dishes, reflecting its own resident community's specific preferences.

Interaction with other Alderbridge policies

This policy works alongside the Health and Safety Policy (governing food hygiene and safe kitchen practice) and the Care Planning Policy (governing how a dietary need is documented in the resident's wider care plan).

Worked example

A worked example illustrates that the substance is unchanged from the previous version. A new resident is admitted with a known nut allergy. This is recorded immediately and communicated to the kitchen before their first meal, and every subsequent meal prepared for them is checked against this record — the same process the previous version described in slightly more formal terms.

Frequently asked questions

**Did the actual menu cycle or review frequency change in this version?** No, only the wording was clarified; the four-week cycle and twice-yearly consultation are identical to the previous version. **Can a resident request a meal outside the current rotating menu?** Yes, where practicable, an alternative is offered, particularly for a resident with a specific dietary need the standard menu does not fully address.

Training and competency

Kitchen staff complete allergen awareness training, refreshed annually, alongside general food hygiene training.

Monitoring and compliance

Menu compliance and allergen record accuracy are reviewed by the registered manager as part of routine kitchen checks.

Record keeping and retention

Dietary and allergen records are retained in the resident's care record per the Records Retention Schedule.

Approval and review history

This policy was approved by the Chief Executive on 1 April 2025 and this version took effect, superseding the earlier wording.

Contractor and third-party premises

Where Alderbridge staff work temporarily on premises it does not own or control — for example,
accompanying a resident to a hospital appointment, or a community support worker visiting a person's own
home — this statement's underlying commitment to reasonably practicable safety still applies, but the
specific control measures available differ from an Alderbridge-owned site; staff are expected to use
professional judgement about what is achievable in that setting and to report back any recurring concern
(for example, a specific home visit location that repeatedly presents a hazard) so it can be reflected in that
person's own individual risk assessment going forward.

Budgeting for health and safety

Health and safety improvement work is treated as a distinct, protected line within each site's annual budget
rather than something competing directly against other operational spending decisions made site by site;
the Health and Safety Lead reviews proposed spend against the incident and audit data described above,
so that investment is directed toward the risks the evidence actually shows are most significant, rather
than toward whichever concern was most recently or most vocally raised.

Lone Worker Devices Policy

Supersedes the version effective 1 July 2024. Adds a mandatory check-in call at the start and end of each lone visit, in addition to the device; extends device issuance to a night-shift single-staffed site role.

Purpose and scope

This policy sets out how Alderbridge Care Group protects a staff member working alone, including a community visit and, newly in this version, a single-staffed night shift. It applies to every community-visiting role and every single-staffed night-shift role.

Policy statement

A lone worker is issued a device with a panic button and GPS location, now paired with a mandatory check-in call at the start and end of each period of lone working, providing a second, active layer of protection alongside the device's own passive availability.

Definitions

**Lone worker device** the issued device combining a panic button and GPS location tracking. **Mandatory check-in call** the new requirement, introduced in this version, for a lone worker to call a designated contact at the start and end of their lone-working period. **Single-staffed night shift** a night shift covered by only one staff member on site, now eligible for device issuance for the first time in this version.

Roles and responsibilities

**A lone worker**, whether community-visiting or on a single-staffed night shift, carries their device and makes the new mandatory check-in call at the start and end of each lone-working period. **A designated contact** receives the check-in call and escalates if an expected call does not arrive within a defined window. **The registered manager** ensures every eligible staff member, now including a single-staffed night role, holds an issued, working device.

specialist input for a prospective resident with complex needs.

1. Complete a face-to-face pre-admission assessment before agreeing any non-emergency admission,
covering care needs, risk, and compatibility with the site's current resident group.

2. Complete a documented mental capacity screen as part of every pre-admission assessment, a new
mandatory step introduced in this version.

3. Make a home-manager phone call to the prospective resident's current GP as part of the assessment,
discussing relevant clinical history.

4. For a non-emergency admission, the full written GP summary must be received before admission
proceeds; the previous allowance for same-day admission pending only the phone call has been removed.

5. Only an admission meeting the defined emergency placement criteria may proceed ahead of the full
written GP summary, with the summary followed up and reviewed within 72 hours.

6. Confirm the site can meet the prospective resident's specific needs, including any specialist equipment
or staffing ratio required, before admission is agreed.

7. Share the completed assessment, including the mental capacity screen outcome, with the care team
before the resident's first day.

Where a prospective resident is being discharged from hospital with limited notice, the registered manager
may still accept a condensed assessment focused on immediate safety needs under the emergency
placement route specifically, with the fuller assessment, GP summary and mental capacity screen
completed within the first 72 hours of admission.

Local and regional variations

Harbour View, with its larger nursing capacity, completes an additional clinical review by its lead nurse as
part of the pre-admission assessment for a prospective resident with complex nursing needs, beyond the
standard assessment used at other sites.

Interaction with other Alderbridge policies

This policy works alongside the Care Planning Policy (governing how the assessment translates into the
resident's initial care plan), the Infection Prevention and Control Policy (governing any pre-admission
screening this raises), and the Mental Capacity Act guidance (governing how the new capacity screen is
conducted).
